description: An object identifier in the URL/body is incremented or swapped for a sibling value belonging to a different user/tenant, while authenticated as the original user, to check whether the server enforces ownership checks.
detection_method: Comparative analysis (idor.py): same path-shape with a different ID, under two distinct authorization contexts, both returning a structurally similar successful response.

description: A known redirect-shaped parameter (next, return_url, redirect, etc.) is set to an external URL to test whether the application redirects there without validating the target host.
detection_method: open_redirect.py: redirect_chain's final hop resolves to a host outside the request's own origin and matches the supplied parameter value.

description: An arbitrary Origin header is sent with a request to check whether the server reflects it back in Access-Control-Allow-Origin while also allowing credentials.
detection_method: security_headers.py: Access-Control-Allow-Origin equals the sent Origin AND Access-Control-Allow-Credentials is true, or a wildcard origin is combined with credentials.

description: A captured JWT's header 'alg' field is checked against whether the server accepts an unsigned ('none') or algorithm-confused token, bypassing signature verification.
detection_method: Requires crafting a structurally valid but unsigned/mismatched-algorithm token and observing whether an otherwise-authenticated endpoint accepts it -- a clear binary signal, but only ever done against explicitly in-scope, authorized test accounts.

description: A captured JWT's HMAC signature is checked against a small, well-known wordlist of common/default secrets to see whether the signing key is weak or default.
detection_method: Offline verification against a candidate secret list; a match means any party knowing that secret can forge valid tokens. Performed only against tokens issued to the tester's own authorized test account.

description: Repeated authentication attempts against a login/OTP/password-reset endpoint, within the assessment's configured rate limit, to check whether the server throttles or locks out after repeated failures.
detection_method: A configured number of sequential failed attempts (bounded by the assessment's own rate_limit setting) all return the same non-lockout response.

description: An extra, undocumented but plausible field (e.g. role, is_admin, price) is added to a create/update JSON request body to test whether the server blindly binds all submitted fields to the underlying object.
detection_method: A follow-up read of the created/updated object shows the extra field was persisted with the attacker-supplied value, not the server-assigned default.

description: An API response is checked for fields that go beyond what the corresponding UI displays (internal IDs, hashed credentials, other users' PII), suggesting the backend relies on the client to filter sensitive data.
detection_method: Structural inspection of the JSON response body for field names matching sensitive-data patterns (password, hash, ssn, token, secret) that are not rendered anywhere in the associated UI.

description: A standard GraphQL introspection query is sent to check whether the schema (including fields not exposed in the client app) is disclosed in production.
detection_method: Response to the introspection query returns a full schema document rather than an error or restricted response.

description: A single GraphQL request batching many nested/aliased queries is sent, within the assessment's rate/concurrency limits, to check whether the server enforces query depth/cost limiting.
detection_method: Response timing and resource usage scale disproportionately with query complexity, with no query-cost rejection from the server.

description: A file upload endpoint is tested with a benign file using an alternate extension, double extension, or manipulated Content-Type to check whether server-side extension/type validation can be bypassed.
detection_method: The upload is accepted (2xx) and the file is reachable at a predictable, publicly-fetchable URL -- content itself stays inert/benign (e.g. a plain text marker), never an executable payload.

description: A serialized-object-shaped parameter (often base64-encoded) is probed with a malformed-but-harmless variant of the expected type to see whether the server attempts to deserialize arbitrary class graphs rather than a fixed schema.
detection_method: A distinct deserialization-error stack trace/signature appears (as opposed to a generic validation error), indicating the input reached a generic deserializer before type-checking.

description: A JSON body with a '__proto__' or 'constructor.prototype' key is submitted to an endpoint that recursively merges/clones input, to test whether it pollutes the global Object prototype.
detection_method: A follow-up, unrelated request to the same application shows an unexpected property present on objects that should not have it -- confirming prototype-level contamination, not just acceptance of the input.
